_strings.@@2546055790fa: Treaty conformity — MS does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by MS. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Mississippi does NOT conform to federal tax treaties and re-taxes treaty-exempt income. Two .gov findings establish this. (1) The MS DOR Individual Income Tax FAQ states verbatim: "Does Mississippi honor federal income tax exemption treaties between the United States and other foreign counties? No, as a general rule, Mississippi does not follow federal income tax exemption treaties. Any income earned on a 1042S should be reported on the Mississippi return as taxable income." (2) Unlike most states, MS does NOT start from federal AGI — the 2023 Form 80-105 builds Mississippi income from scratch line-by-line (wages, business income, capital gain, interest, dividends, pensions, etc. on lines 38-48; "Total income" line 49) and then applies MS-specific adjustments (lines 50-65) to reach "Mississippi adjusted gross income" (line 66). Because the return is built from gross income items rather than inheriting the federal AGI exclusion, treaty-exempt wages/income (e.g., reported on a 1042-S) are pulled into Mississippi taxable income directly; no special add-back schedule is needed. Net effect: treaty-exempt income IS taxed by Mississippi, so conforms_to_federal_treaties = false.

Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Mississippi adjusted gross income: 2023 Form 80-105 (resident return), page 1, line 13, which is carried from page 2, line 66 'Mississippi adjusted gross income (line 49 minus line 65)'. Mississippi does NOT start from federal AGI — the return builds MS income from its own line items (wages line 38 through other income line 48, totaled at line 49) minus MS adjustments (lines 50-65). Do NOT supply federal AGI. The pack ships the subtractions to get from line 13 to line 16 'Mississippi taxable income' for a standard-deduction filer: the shipped standard_deduction for each status is the SUM of the MS standard deduction and the MS filing-status exemption (see notes), and the shipped dependent exemption is $1,500 each; the rate schedule then reproduces line 17. Itemizers (Form 80-108 Schedule A) and nonresident/part-year filers (Form 80-205, which prorates deductions and exemptions) must be computed on the form instead. Adjudication note (two-pass): exemptions_count must be 0 — the Mississippi per-status personal exemption ($6,000 single/MFS, $12,000 MFJ, $8,000 Head of Family) is FOLDED INTO the shipped standard_deduction amounts (see modeling note), never applied per count. Only dependents_count is applied ($1,500 each). 2023 Mississippi rates (instructions p.22, 'Tax Rates'): 0% on the first $10,000.00 of taxable income and 5% on taxable income in excess of $10,000.00. ONE schedule covers ALL filing statuses (the Schedule of Tax Computation, p.27, has no per-status columns for rates); it is duplicated per status here. MODELING NOTE — shipped standard_deduction is a COMBINED per-status amount: Mississippi's personal exemption is a fixed per-FILING-STATUS amount (Single $6,000; Married Filing Joint/Combined $12,000; Married Filing Separate $6,000 per spouse; Head of Family $8,000), not a per-person amount, so it cannot be shipped as a 'personal' per-item exemption (Head of Family's $8,000 is not $6,000 x any count). The shipped standard_deduction = MS standard deduction + MS filing-status exemption: Single $2,300 + $6,000 = $8,300; MFJ $4,600 + $12,000 = $16,600; MFS $2,300 + $6,000 = $8,300; Head of Family $3,400 + $8,000 = $11,400. No 'personal' exemption key is shipped, so exemptions_count has no effect. Corroboration: the booklet's own filing thresholds (p.5) are exactly these sums — 'Single... gross income in excess of $8,300 plus $1,500 for each dependent; Married... in excess of $16,600 plus $1,500 for each dependent.' MARRIED COMBINED RETURN (two-column) math is NOT modeled — can OVERSTATE tax by up to $500 for two-income couples: on a combined return where both spouses have positive taxable income (Form 80-105 columns A and B), the Schedule of Tax Computation line 1 gives EACH column its own first $10,000 (or part) at 0%, so up to $20,000 of the couple's combined taxable income is taxed at 0%. This pack's single-base married_filing_jointly computation gives only one $10,000 zero band and matches the form only when all income is in Column A (one-income couple / true joint return). If one column is positive and the other negative, the form nets them in Column A; if both are negative, no tax is due. MARRIED FILING SEPARATELY: Form 80-105 line 15 instruction — 'Enter the amount from line 12. If Married-Filing Separate, divide this amount by 2.' Each MFS spouse gets exactly half the total authorized exemptions (($12,000 + $1,500 x dependents)/2 = $6,000 + $750 per dependent), and any unused portion of one spouse's standard deduction ($2,300) or exemption ($6,000) may NOT be used by the other spouse. The shipped $8,300 is exact for MFS with zero dependents; with dependents the shipped $1,500/dependent overstates the exemption by $750 each — compute on the form. If one MFS spouse itemizes, the other must also itemize. Head of Family (Mississippi's head-of-household status) REQUIRES at least one dependent living in the home the entire year; that required dependent is listed on line 6, counted on line 7/9, and DOES receive the $1,500 dependent exemption (p.7: '$8,000 on line 11 and $1,500 for the required dependent... totals $9,500') — pass it in dependents_count. Qualifying surviving spouse mapping: Mississippi's 'Married - Spouse Died in Tax Year (2023)' status uses the identical $12,000 exemption and $4,600 standard deduction as Married Filing Joint/Combined, so it maps cleanly to married_filing_jointly. Mississippi has no multi-year qualifying-surviving-spouse status. Age 65-or-over and blind additional exemptions ($1,500 per box checked, taxpayer and spouse only, Form 80-105 line 8) are base reductions but are NOT applied by calc.state_tax — take them on the form (they are shipped as informational 'age_65'/'blind' keys only). Itemized deductions: filers may itemize on Form 80-108 Schedule A instead of the standard deduction (state income taxes and MS gaming losses are NOT deductible); this pack assumes the standard deduction. Tax CREDITS are not modeled: line 18 credit for income tax paid to another state (Form 80-160) and line 19 other credits (Form 80-401 — e.g. new-for-2023 Dependent Care Credit code 37 = 25% of the federal credit for federal AGI <= $50,000, Child Adoption Credit code 25) are subtracted from line 17 tax AFTER the rate schedule; they are credits, not exemptions. Consumer use tax (line 21, 7%) and catastrophe savings tax (line 22, additional 2.5% on non-qualified distributions) are separate additions on the return and are NOT part of the line 17 income tax this pack computes. No tax-table mandate: Mississippi has no lookup-table requirement — every filer computes line 17 with the Schedule of Tax Computation (p.27) bracket math, so the pack's marginal math matches the form exactly. Rounding: the booklet mandates whole-dollar rounding (p.22, 'Round to the Nearest Dollar': round down under $.50, up at $.50 and over) — identical to the engine's round-half-up. 2023 legislative context (HB 531, 2022 session, p.3 'What's New'): beginning tax year 2023 no tax is levied on taxable income up to and including $10,000; the printed 2023 rate on the excess is 5% (p.22). HB 531 schedules future cuts on the excess over $10,000: 4.7% (2024), 4.4% (2025), 4.0% (2026) — those rates do NOT apply to 2023. There was no mid-year 2023 rate change; the 2023 filing-season schedule is 0%/$10,000 then 5%. The Schedule of Tax Computation prints no '$X + Y% of excess over $Z' additive constants, so there is no rounded-constant divergence to quantify. Nonresidents and part-year residents file Form 80-205 (taxable income line 19, tax line 20) and must PRORATE deductions and exemptions by the MS-income ratio — this pack models only the full-year resident Form 80-105.
